item.title: Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list in firefight that left 11 dead
item.description: Mexico’s military announced on Saturday that it had captured a drug kingpin on the FBI’s list of 10 most wanted fugitives in an operation that left four soldiers and seven suspected gunmen dead. Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “Chapo Isidro,” was captured on Friday night during a special forces raid in the northwestern state of Sinaloa, along with his alleged second-in-command and a financial operator for his criminal organisation. item.title: Why a slow-paced show about broken friendships is China’s antidote to AI fatigue
item.description: A slow-paced Chinese reality show about fractured friendships has proved an unexpected cultural phenomenon, sparking a nationwide reckoning over huorengan – the messy, unscripted sense of being alive – as AI companions and algorithm-driven microdramas flourish. The show’s emotional power is distilled in a viral scene when two women who barely spoke to each other for seven years sit across a small wooden table. item.title: Indonesia, EU sign ‘ambitious’ trade deal

item.title: Asian Gaelic Games brings 2-day celebration of all things Irish to Hong Kong
item.description: More than 700 amateur athletes from Ireland and across the region descended on Hong Kong for the Asian Gaelic Games on Saturday, as the city played host to the annual sporting tournament’s 30th anniversary. Participants celebrated the atmosphere and camaraderie on display, praising the city’s hosting of the milestone tournament as organisers pointed to the growth of Irish sports among both expatriates and local communities across Asia. item.description: The just-concluded Apec summit in Shenzhen showcased China’s role as a regional leader, state news agency Xinhua said on Saturday, casting the city’s rapid rise as a model for an “Asia-Pacific miracle” under Chinese guidance.
